node.2a6321b4ce90763bf0be564e puts offering in Scope; node.6d6e7adc6faa9d94b74c08e5, node.968dbccb08282a4e8a580ae5, node.97af37a2579f59b0ee43211f and node.bca408c75cbf8467afafada6 put promotional conditions in Scope. False conditions return OUT_OF_SCOPE rather than FALSE for prohibition or TRUE for selected-control compliance. Both an applicability interpretation and a substantive-condition interpretation remain possible; the question domain needs to resolve this distinction.

The two offer-level candidates combine an offer-level promotional connection with existence of a non-discount gift component. In mixed offers, the same gift component must have the required promotional connection. Otherwise the formulas could impose an unsupported restriction on an unrelated component.

Unit db43e253bea18.u0.2 defines distributors as intermediaries distributing SFC-authorised funds. Broader candidate wording must retain this source scope; broader application of paragraph 3.11 requires separate support.

Unit db43e253bea18.u12.2646 says guaranteed returns or incentives may be considered gifts. Neither automatic gift classification nor automatic exemption follows. Supplied classification judgments are not implemented by the formulas, and gift-control compliance is not overall regulatory compliance.

node.bc55be7e973a689d07f9e64b correctly focuses on attributed offering, but categorical independence from funding and fulfilment is not expressly resolved for all third-party arrangements. The source identifies offering as the operative act without requiring completed payment.

No external dependencies are supplied. Independent validation beyond the circular would require the applicable Code of Conduct paragraph 3.11 and question 1 of the SFC FAQ issued on 30 September 2010; broader advertising validation would require paragraph 2.3, the Advertising Guidelines Applicable to Collective Investment Schemes Authorized under the Product Codes and applicable supplements. Verification of the underlying disclosure duty would require section 6.4 of the Handbook's Overarching Principles. These missing authorities are not necessary to establish the three narrow, express circular claims assessed here.

The supplied source establishes no concrete operative date interval or historical versions of external authorities. Runtime temporal uncertainty semantics do not establish the applicable legal version.
